events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts the second petition
events.body: In the burial club's room at Baile thais, Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts the second petition over three nights by a single coal lamp, with Griogal and two others reading each page back to her aloud. She writes its last sentence twice before settling the wording Griogal judges means it rather than asks permission to mean it.

events.title: Tormod Buidhe's sister's boy dies of the grey fever
events.body: A boy not yet old enough for his first wage dies of the grey fever at Baile thais under Eilidh nic Raghnaill's sitting, having asked her, near the end, what month it was. His mother keeps his name from the burial club's book, and Eilidh does not ask for it twice.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins the burial club's book
events.body: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins keeping a plain hand-written record for the burial club at Baile thais, answering to no custodian's roll, after watching her father Raghnall Breac carry twenty years of names in his memory and give none of them to paper. She means not to do the same.

events.title: The Company dismisses Coinneach Ruadh at his own store
events.body: The Company's agent at Cnoc dhìreach delivers Coinneach Ruadh's letter of dismissal at the store's door in front of the week's flour queue, the day his signature to the second petition dries. He is offered twice the chance to withdraw his name and twice declines it, saying a name once given is not the giver's to take back.

events.title: The first constables' company reaches Baile thais
events.body: Forty constables under an officer named Prosser march into Baile thais on the twenty-fifth of Gearran and wall the settlement's old open store within the fortnight, taking the camp's well inside the new wall. Eilidh nic Raghnaill and the burial club watch the company make camp on ground that had been common land that same morning.

events.title: An overman gives up his cot at Cathair gheal
events.body: In the crowded shared ward at Cathair gheal a Dia-thìreach overman of the north-west galleries gives up his own bed to a human boy of the concession no more than nine years old, and sits the night on the floor beside him. Hannah Webb writes of it to Eilidh nic Raghnaill at Baile thais.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill reads Ìomhar Seabhag's sermon to the Lamp-Watch
events.body: A fowler leaves a written copy of Ìomhar Seabhag's Seann Skell sermon with the burial club's door-keeper at Baile thais, and Eilidh nic Raghnaill reads it aloud to the room by the same lamp she drafted the second petition by. For once she does not write anything in the club's book afterward.

events.title: Aonghas takes the loft at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: A crew-leader from Baile thais asks Aonghas, keeper of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr since Seònaid Bhàn's line came to him, whether the loft above his stable might hold men now and again with no questions asked. He agrees, and stops in time asking what they carry.

events.title: Coinneach nan Ràmh's word on the loft at the Reòta
events.body: The old fisherman Coinneach nan Ràmh tells Aonghas that the loft at An Taigh-seinnse Reòta is never once found empty by the Company's carters passing through, and never once holds the same men two nights running: it comes and goes, he says, like the tide, and no man has ever caught the tide at its turning.

events.title: A boy of Àth fhiadhaich at Aonghas's door
events.body: A boy runner out of Àth fhiadhaich comes soaked from the ford into Aonghas's yard, asks for bread as any boy might, and leaves a folded scrap under the loose board by the stable door naming a date and nothing else. Aonghas burns it in the kitchen fire that night.

events.title: The fire on Cnoc an Rabhaidh
events.body: On 27 am Màrt, Aonghas watches smoke rise thin from Cnoc an Rabhaidh in a hard north-west wind, and every wheel within sight of his yard stops within the hour. A carter in his own yard names it a heath fire before anyone learns otherwise.

events.title: The heather burned thin
events.body: The constables burn the heather of Cnoc an Rabhaidh to deny the hill a second beacon. It grows back thin and late the following spring, and three years pass before anyone on the coal road speaks openly of what the fire had truly been.

events.title: Tormod Buabhall's word on a house with nothing left to guard
events.body: Meeting Aonghas at the horse-fair after the ships have thinned to nothing, Tormod Buabhall tells him a house with no custom left keeps its gates shut for a different reason than before: a house that guards everything still has, behind its locked door, something it means to keep.

events.title: Strake's commission read without the council's name
events.body: At Ros dhomhain, Aonghas stands in the market square while Lionel Strake's commission is read from the Residency's steps: it names the Company and the Administration in an Tìr Thall, and, for the first time in any Commissioner's commission, does not name the Council of Custodians at all.

events.title: The iron bird seen over Muileann chrom
events.body: A flying machine passes twice over the Muileann chrom valley without beating its wings, and the crews at the pit-mouth stop their barrows to watch it go. By evening the district has a name for it, eun-iarainn, borrowed from nowhere and understood at once.

events.title: The old man of Doire mhòr
events.body: An old man carried gently from his own doorstone by constables clearing houses under the edict of seizure asks only that it be written down that they were gentle about it. Mòrag nic Iain Maor, come from Muileann chrom, carries the sentence home with no book to hand.

events.title: Sìneag's ride to Muileann chrom
events.body: Sìneag, custodian of the camp at Baile dhomhain, rides to the steward's house at Muileann chrom to ask whether the overseer's staff can answer for the two streets pulled down for the new spoil-tip. Mòrag nic Iain Maor can offer her nothing that year.

events.title: The order for the third and fourth rows
events.body: A printed order reaches Muileann chrom's overseer naming eleven households of the camp's third and fourth rows for clearance before the new gallery mouth. The Company's agent Osgood carries it to Mòrag nic Iain Maor's door, and carries her answer back unwritten.

events.title: Coinneach Ruadh brings word of the guild's rifles
events.body: Coinneach Ruadh, riding the district roads with unpaid news since his clerkship was taken, brings Mòrag nic Iain Maor word of the silver guild's rifles and of a single council the custodians and priests mean to hold in the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag before autumn.

events.title: Coinneach Ruadh's ride of the twentieth
events.body: Coinneach Ruadh rides into Muileann chrom on the twentieth of an Gearran with word that the grievance is called across every mining district at once, and that the Residency has already had its answer that morning from Muileann chrom and Baile thais both.

events.title: The beacons of the coal country answer
events.body: On the night war is called, signal fires long kept secret are carried openly to every beacon height the mining districts hold, ridge answering ridge from Doire mhòr to the silver hills, the first time the whole coal country has shown itself lit at once.
